items.prompt: Distinguish between a consumer durable and a producer good using the two freezer purchases. A household buys a freezer for its food; a meal business buys a freezer to support production. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Consumer products are bought for personal or household use; producer goods are bought by businesses to make other goods or services; they include capital goods such as machinery and equipment, and materials or components used up in production. Durable goods are used repeatedly over time, while non-durable goods are used up more quickly. Services provide an activity or benefit rather than ownership of a new physical good. Classify using purpose and characteristics: the same item can be a household consumer durable or business equipment depending on who buys it and why. The categories can overlap because they answer different questions. The first is a consumer durable, the second business equipment or a capital good. Both are physical durable items; buying purpose changes the consumer/producer distinction.
marking_guidance: Difference: Consumer products are bought for personal or household use; producer goods are bought by businesses to make other goods or services; they include capital goods such as machinery and equipment, and materials or components used up in production.

items.prompt: Draw a labelled product-life-cycle model with sales and time axes and explain its stages. Construct an illustrative life cycle for a lunch-container range, with no numerical sales data provided. [6]
items.canonical_answer:
Put time on the horizontal axis and sales on the vertical axis. Draw low introductory sales, a rising growth section, a high flatter maturity section and a declining section. Label the stages so the reader can distinguish the changes in the sales pattern. Some descriptions distinguish saturation within the mature plateau. The curve is conceptual unless data are supplied; do not present it as actual measured sales or assume a given number of years per stage. Extension actions such as adapting the product or finding new buyers can sometimes prolong sales but do not guarantee revival. ![Product life cycle](diagrams/product-life-cycle.png)

The labelled diagram shows the model’s changing sales direction rather than forecasts for a real range. Maturity does not mean zero sales, and decline is falling sales rather than necessarily an immediate end to all demand.
marking_guidance: Input: Put time on the horizontal axis and sales on the vertical axis.

items.prompt: Distinguish between the name, image and loyalty in Oru’s bag example. Oru Gear names its bag “Tana”. Buyers associate it with durability and some repeatedly choose it. [6]
items.canonical_answer: A brand name identifies an offering and distinguishes it from competitors. Brand loyalty is repeated preference and purchasing of that brand. Brand image is the identity or impression associated with it. A business can choose a name and communicate an intended image, but customers’ actual experiences influence the image they hold. Recognition is not itself loyalty: someone may know the name and still buy a rival. A strong image can support differentiation, but it needs credible quality and service rather than unsupported claims. Tana is the name; the durability association is image; repeated choice is loyalty. They are connected but not definitions of the same thing.
marking_guidance: Difference: A brand name identifies an offering and distinguishes it from competitors.

items.prompt: Explain how Nela’s container and label perform two distinct packaging functions. Nela Soup uses a secure food container and a clear label showing contents and handling information. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Packaging is the physical container or wrapping for a product, also used for promotional purposes. It can protect contents, contain portions, preserve quality, make handling and transport easier, supply instructions or information and support recognition on display. Explain the function and consequence: a secure seal reduces leakage, while a readable label helps correct use. Packaging adds cost and waste, so the design should fit the product and customer need. Saying product or promotion does not explain what the container actually does. Containment reduces spills during the journey; information helps customers use and identify the meal. A colourful logo can help recognition but does not by itself explain protection.
marking_guidance: Starting point: Packaging is the physical container or wrapping for a product, also used for promotional purposes.

items.prompt: Explain why a low initial entry price and a high skimming price suit different conditions. Teya Drink enters a competitive local market with a familiar product, while Omi Devices introduces a distinctive design valued by a small early market. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Penetration pricing sets a low initial price to encourage customers to try a product and to win market share. Price skimming sets a high initial price for a distinctive new product that some buyers will pay more for, and the price is often reduced later. Teya enters a competitive market with a familiar product, so a low entry price may attract trial, provided Teya can afford the low margin. Omi’s distinctive design is valued by a small early market, so skimming may suit Omi, but only while the distinctive benefit supports the higher price and rivals cannot copy it quickly.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: penetration = low initial price for trial and share; skimming = high initial price for a distinctive new product.
Context: Teya faces competition with a familiar product; Omi has a distinctive design valued by a small early market.
Effect: each strategy suits only under its condition (affordable margin; benefit not quickly copied).

items.prompt: Explain why Ota should check customer response as well as use its cost-plus rule. Ota Cups adds a 20% mark-up to full unit cost. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Cost-plus pricing adds a specified mark-up to an appropriate unit-cost base. It offers a clear starting rule and can cover the included cost if the resulting price is actually paid, but ignores demand and rival prices if used alone. A wrong or incomplete cost base can mislead. Mark-up is on cost; margin is on sales revenue. The rule is straightforward, but the business must check whether buyers accept the resulting price and whether costs remain accurate.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Cost-plus pricing adds a specified mark-up to an appropriate unit-cost base.

items.prompt: Explain how penetration pricing can attract Teya’s trial buyers and create a risk. Teya Juice enters a competitive local market and can supply a limited trial at a low introductory price. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Penetration pricing uses a low initial price to encourage entry, trial and market share. It may suit a familiar product with strong competition and price-sensitive buyers if the firm can finance the low return and supply the extra demand. It risks weak margins, a low-price image and customers resisting later rises. Extra volume is not guaranteed and more sales do not automatically mean more profit. The low entry price may encourage switching, but the owner should monitor margins and capacity and explain any later normal price clearly.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Penetration pricing uses a low initial price to encourage entry, trial and market share.

items.prompt: Explain why Hena’s distinctiveness matters to a skimming strategy. Hena Devices has a new design valued by a small group of early buyers and few close substitutes initially. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Price skimming uses a high initial price for a new distinctive offering where early buyers are willing to pay, often lowering it later as the market develops. It may help recover development spending and capture a high return per early unit. It requires credible differentiation and can attract competitors or restrict demand. A high price without a valued distinctive benefit is not enough. Skimming may suit that early demand, but the firm should reassess as rivals appear rather than assume the high price can continue indefinitely.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Price skimming uses a high initial price for a new distinctive offering where early buyers are willing to pay, often lowering it later as the market develops.

items.prompt: Explain how rival prices can inform Oru without replacing its own cost assessment. Oru Stationery compares prices for a standard notebook sold by several local shops. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Competitive pricing uses rival prices as a reference when setting the firm’s price. It can help where customers compare similar offerings, but the firm’s costs, quality and service may differ. Matching a rival below a sustainable cost can harm the business. It does not mean every firm must charge exactly the same amount or ignore differentiation. A similar price can avoid an unexplained premium, while availability or service may justify some difference. Check Oru’s own cost before matching a rival.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Competitive pricing uses rival prices as a reference when setting the firm’s price.

items.prompt: Explain how Nela’s temporary offer can affect sales timing and return. Nela Cases offers one week’s discount on its established range. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Promotional pricing offers a temporary reduced or special price to stimulate a response, such as trial or clearing suitable stock. It differs from a continuing low entry strategy in its temporary promotional purpose. It reduces revenue per unit and may bring purchases forward rather than create lasting demand. Clear duration and conditions matter, and repeated offers can train customers to wait for discounts. The temporary offer may encourage purchases now, but management should compare added contribution and promotion cost rather than equate more units with higher profit.
marking_guidance: Knowledge: Promotional pricing offers a temporary reduced or special price to stimulate a response, such as trial or clearing suitable stock.

items.prompt: Explain how advertising and personal selling differ for Nara’s complex tool. Nara Tools compares a local advert with direct explanation of a complex tool to business buyers. [6]
items.canonical_answer: Advertising communicates a paid promotional message through a medium. Sales promotion provides a usually short-term incentive such as a discount, sample or coupon. Personal selling involves direct interaction to explain an offering and respond to questions. Public relations manages relationships and reputation through appropriate communication and activities. A radio station is an advertising medium, not a separate promotion type equivalent to personal selling. An advert can build awareness across an audience, while personal selling can handle detailed individual questions. The time and cost per contact may make direct selling unnecessary for a simple low-price everyday item.

items.prompt: Explain why Omi Bags’ bag design is a product decision while cutting and stitching are production activities. [6]

items.canonical_answer: A marketing plan sets a target, objective and coordinated product, price, promotion and distribution decisions, with resources, actions and review. The elements should reinforce the same need: a premium fragile product, bargain price, mass discount message and unreliable handling would conflict. Specify enough to act and monitor results, while treating sales expectations as assumptions to test. Marketing planning sits inside the broader business plan and must fit capacity and finance. Model plan: target local tradespeople needing durable organised storage; objective—test paid demand and repeat interest over four weeks within current capacity. Product—durable tool bag with practical compartments and clear care information. Price—test N$120 against N$80 stated unit cost, review actual uptake and costs. Promotion—local demonstration and a concise accessible notice explaining the benefit and collection arrangements. Distribution—direct workshop collection, recording orders to avoid exceeding capacity. Action/review—owner confirms material supply, schedules a small trial, records paid units and feedback weekly and revises the offer before expansion. This is a connected plan, not four unrelated definitions.

Normal price = 80 + 40 = N$120. Discount = 120 × 0.25 = N$30. Promotional price = 120 − 30 = N$90. The customer saving is N$30 and the price remains N$10 above the stated unit cost before any new campaign cost. d Sampling directly addresses uncertain taste among relevant local buyers, while the broad campaign mainly adds awareness they already have. Samples cost money and do not prove paid demand, but a controlled trial limits that exposure. Prefer sampling with clear price and purchase information, then review conversion; choose wider advertising if evidence later shows lack of awareness is the actual barrier.

items.prompt:
Tula Tea has full unit cost N$80 and uses a 50% mark-up on cost for its normal price. It considers a temporary 25% reduction from that price. Local buyers know where to buy but are unsure about the new flavour. Controlled sampling at its collection point is affordable; a broad campaign costs much more. No increase in paid demand is yet confirmed.

a Explain how Tula’s pricing and promotion choices interact with its stated customer barrier and costs. [8]
b Evaluate a temporary price cut against controlled sampling as the next step. [12]
items.canonical_answer: a Cost-plus gives N$120 normal price; the 25% reduction gives N$90 and reduces the amount above stated unit cost from N$40 to N$10. More units would therefore be needed to preserve a given surplus before new campaign costs, and no volume increase is confirmed. Sampling addresses taste uncertainty directly; a price cut may not resolve that uncertainty. Promotion should fit the actual barrier and preserve feasible supply. b A lower price could encourage trial but reduces the return on each sold unit and may attract temporary bargain demand. Controlled sampling lets buyers experience the flavour without reducing the price on every qualifying sale, although samples and administration cost money. Given known location and uncertain taste, start with an affordable limited sample trial, measure paid conversion and reassess price evidence. Do not claim higher profit merely from a lower price or count samples as sales. If affordability proves decisive, test a sustainable price response instead.

a Evaluate the promotion options at Omi under the original facts. [12]

items.canonical_answer: a Affordable sampling addresses the unknown taste, whereas a broad awareness campaign spends on a need already met. A discount from N$50 to N$45 reduces the surplus above stated unit cost from N$15 to N$10 without proving it solves the barrier. Prefer a controlled tasting trial and measure paid demand, recognising sample cost and capacity. b Taste is now known and liked, so more sampling has less diagnostic value. A price test or revised value proposition becomes more relevant. The 10% offer still leaves N$10 above the stated cost before extra promotion costs, but profit depends on volume and total costs. Test a limited sustainable price response and review paid sales rather than promise a permanent discount. The recommendation changes because the demonstrated barrier changes, not because price cuts are universally effective.
